summary.motive: Attack the perimeter's leverage math: pin every down defender with interior blockers, then outnumber the edge with tandem pulling guards, a fullback, and an arcing wing.
summary.keyDefender: Force Player (SAM) — caught between spilling the sweep and boxing the edge
summary.whyItWorks: The pins guarantee no interior defender can pursue, so the defense’s edge support must handle three separate blockers arriving in sequence; any hesitation between spill and box leaves the corner turned.
summary.failureMode: A defensive end who fights across the pin’s face, or a force player who commits instantly to one answer and lets the second puller be blocked by design rather than by reaction.

beats.title: 1. The Pins Set the Trap
beats.text: Four interior blockers — tackle, center, right guard’s replacement, tight end — each drive their man down and inward. Not one defender on the line of scrimmage can pursue; the entire front is erased before a single puller moves.

beats.title: 2. Tandem Pull Around the Wreckage
beats.text: Both guards pull in tandem through the vacuum: the left guard kicks, the right guard leads. This is leverage math — two pullers against a defense that has zero unblocked linemen to disrupt them.

beats.title: 3. Force Player in Conflict
beats.text: The SAM must spill or box — and he hesitates between the two, which means he does neither well. The kicking guard catches him mid-decision and spills him out of the play entirely.

beats.title: 4. Convoy Turns the Corner
beats.text: The fullback and arcing wing form a moving convoy with the safety and force corner already walled. The running back bends off the pin-blocked edge into green grass — Roman trading interior muscle for perimeter leverage.

relations.tell: Both guards pull together around four stationary pins while the QB hands and boots away — no mesh read, no decision, pure numbers sweep.
